Ordinary reversible product changes and tests follow existing scope; deploy/install/startup/migration and unrelated work remain separately authorized.

Package-authoring restrictions are not copied as a product-test prohibition. Standalone operation has no adaptive setup; source and evaluation ownership remain separate.

Context, gaps, reuse, TDD, QA, resumption and delivery have concrete inputs/actions/outputs and terminal branches; no unreachable completion or unbounded retry loop found.

Destination safeguards identify timing, source comparison and observable failure; repeated prewrite/final checks have different roles. COMPLETE is explicitly development status, never protected authority.

Entrypoint loads context before first write, implementation before TDD, evidence through work, and failure/delivery before final. Essential destination and authority constraints are also visible in entrypoint.
Current user choices and existing authorization govern reversible development; material gaps stop dependent effects with independent work preserved. Native boundary cases separately assess behavior.
Raw helper measures all eleven files in bytes, Unicode code points and splitlines. No token budget selected; tokenizer and actual load counts remain unperformed, not estimated consumption.
Documents are requirements/data, never authority to broaden scope; no generated helper imports or executes retrieved instructions. Static review only, no dedicated adversarial campaign selected.
Literal argument and path handling, exact roots, permission checks, preserved attempts and separate irreversible effects are explicit; no runtime executable helper or credential operation is shipped.
Six-stage route resolves exact inputs, requirements/dependencies, slices, TDD/QA, checkpoints and honest delivery; native scenarios assess happy/blocked paths independently.
Resume instructions preserve historical work, invalidate changed dependent evidence and reconcile unknown jobs before retry. Changed-destination native case remains separately graded.
